section.title: Plugins Configuration Dialog
section.para:
This dialog allows user to add new plugins or modify the system ones. It is available in the menu
Edit Configure Plugins
.

The Plugins dialog shows list of all relevant plugins i.e. all installed desktop files that are designated either:
>
Categories=Graphics
Categories=X-Geeqie
The list has the following columns:

listitem.para: If the checkbox is ticked, the plugin will not be displayed in Geeqie menus.
Plugin name as specified in desktop file, and is the name displayed in menus.

the desktop file contains Hidden=TRUE or NoDisplay=TRUE

MimeType list does not contain images
MimeType list is empty and Categories does not contain X-Geeqie

section.title: Adding new plugin
section.para:
New
opens a text editor with a desktop file template. You must amend the line Exec=command %f to contain the command you wish to execute. If it is more than a single command, you must create a script file and call that. If the location of the script file is not in your $PATH environment variable, you must include the full pathname.

section.title: Modifying an existing plugin
section.para:
Edit
opens a text editor with existing desktop file. For desktop files that are not writable by user, it allows saving to a Geeqie specific directory, where it overrides the system file (but only for Geeqie).

section.title: Deleting a plugin
section.para:
Delete
can delete user writable desktop files. System desktop files can't be deleted directly, but it is possible to edit them and set Hidden=TRUE , see above.

section.title: Special plugins
section.para: A desktop file with one of the following names has a special function. It will replace the corresponding internal command.
This can be used for example for a custom trash command or for manipulation of files under version control.

section.title: Geeqie desktop file keys
section.para: Plugins appear in the Plugins menu and in plugin context menus. The legacy X-Geeqie-Menu-Path key does not control menu placement in GTK4; omit it from new desktop files.
To let the user choose a destination folder for a plugin, add this entry to its desktop file: X-Geeqie-Filter=true

The plugin will appear in the Folder action list of the
. Clicking a bookmark uses that folder as the destination. When you run the plugin from the Plugins menu, Geeqie asks you to choose a destination folder.

In the plugin script, use geeqie --get-destination="$file" to get the destination folder with the file's name appended. For example, if the file is /photos/image.jpg and you choose /backup, the command returns /backup/image.jpg. It only returns the path; the script must perform the operation.
for file in "$@"; do destination=$(geeqie --get-destination="$file") printf '%s\n' "$destination" done
The same path is available as $GEEQIE_DESTINATION for the file currently being processed:
printf '%s\n' "$GEEQIE_DESTINATION"
A restart of Geeqie is required for this plugin to be registered
If you want to run a plugin in full-screen mode and wish full-screen to be maintained, include the following entry in the desktop file: X-Geeqie-Keep-Fullscreen=true
Any terminal output from the plugin command can be displayed with the following command: X-Geeqie-Verbose=true
Any terminal output from the plugin command can be displayed, only when multiple files are selected, with the following command: X-Geeqie-Verbose-Multi=true
The plugin can be restricted to run on only certain file types, for example: X-Geeqie-File-Extensions=.jpg; .cr2 The entries are case insensitive.

The key or key combination to execute this function can be set with: X-Geeqie-Hotkey= Key combinations are of the form:
X-Geeqie-Hotkey=<control>y
